data.paper_title: Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects
data.selected_experiment: Table 2, Fama-MacBeth monthly cross-sectional regressions of NYSE stock returns (1964-1997) on lagged ILLIQ (mean-adjusted) and other characteristics

economic_rationale.value: Expected stock return increases with stock illiquidity, because investors require compensation for the price impact of trading.

universe_and_filters.value: NYSE-traded common stocks on CRSP, 1963-1997. A stock is admitted if it has a return in the month, return and volume data for more than 200 days in year y-1, is listed at the end of y-1, has an end-of-year price above $5, has market capitalization data, and its ILLIQ is not in the highest or lowest 1% tail. Returns are adjusted for delistings.

value: market capitalization (SIZE control and listing filter)

signal_formula_words.value: ILLIQ for each stock and year is the average over the year's trading days of the daily absolute return divided by the daily dollar volume. It is then divided by its annual cross-sectional mean across stocks (ILLIQMA).

unresolved_details: No long-short or decile portfolio sort is constructed; the evidence is regression coefficients, so portfolio breakpoints, weighting and a hedge-portfolio return are not stated.
Weighting is not a portfolio weighting; the baseline is OLS across stocks, with weighted least squares as a robustness check whose results are not reported.
Whether the ILLIQ-only specification is the headline is unclear; Table 2 reports specifications with and without additional controls.
Exact definition of the one-year return convention and the timing of stock admission is only partly specified.
Ranking is based on the prior calendar year, so the lag between the end of the formation year and the first return month is not separately specified.
